children: SoftBank’s heavy exposure to artificial intelligence came under pressure after AI leaders called for greater caution in the race to develop more powerful systems

SoftBank Group shares fell more than 13 per cent in Tokyo on Monday, their sharpest decline since late June, after senior artificial intelligence (AI) executives called for a slower approach to developing advanced AI systems.

The fall reflects growing concerns among investors about SoftBank’s large bets on AI. The Japanese investment group is one of the biggest backers of OpenAI, making it particularly sensitive to changes in investor sentiment around the sector.
AI Safety Warnings Weigh On Sentiment
The latest concerns followed calls from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for greater caution around the development of advanced AI models.

The debate has gained attention as AI systems become more capable and companies commit billions of dollars to their development and infrastructure. Investors are now weighing whether the pace of spending and development can be sustained.
The concerns have also affected other AI-linked stocks as markets assess whether greater safety requirements or a slower development cycle could change companies’ growth plans.
The market reaction is particularly important for SoftBank because founder Masayoshi Son has made AI a central part of the group’s investment strategy.

SoftBank has committed billions of dollars to AI companies and infrastructure, with OpenAI among its biggest investments. The group is also looking at opportunities in areas such as robotics and data centres.

The latest decline shows how closely SoftBank’s share price is tied to investor confidence in the AI sector. While companies continue to invest heavily in the technology, questions over valuations, spending and potential returns are becoming more important for investors.
For SoftBank, the challenge will be to convince investors that its large AI investments can deliver returns even as concerns over the pace and safety of AI development grow.
